concept.title: Read the caller-visible contract
paragraphs: Start with the receiver, input types, return type, and accessibility. A return type promises what a successful caller receives; it does not hide failure meaning.
Use IntelliSense one parameter or member at a time rather than memorizing a dense signature.

concept.title: Modern does not automatically mean clearer
paragraphs: Prefer the form that makes this business rule easiest to read and maintain. Older or more explicit syntax can remain the better teaching or production choice.
Compiler diagnostics identify unsupported language versions, inaccessible members, missing required values, and unsafe nullable paths.

lab.title: C# Evolution and Language Milestones
lab.objective: Recognize useful modern C# milestones and verify whether the current toolchain supports them.
lab.task: A small compatibility report maps useful syntax to the configured language version.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/refreshers/r1 from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/refreshers/r1. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/refreshers/r1/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: A small compatibility report maps useful syntax to the configured language version.
Step 4/12: Inspect the project TargetFramework and run dotnet --version.
Step 5/12: Create a tuple array mapping five business-relevant features to their C# versions.
Step 6/12: Print the map with aligned interpolation.
Step 7/12: Write the older explicit array construction form in a comment.
Step 8/12: Use a collection expression for the modern form and explain its shorter intent.
Step 9/12: Temporarily set LangVersion to 11, build to read the collection-expression diagnostic, then restore the project.
Step 10/12: Run the project and record which syntax your configured toolchain accepts.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/refreshers/r1 --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/refreshers/r1 --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
